title.narrative: Svenskt program för Kenyas förbättrade handelsmiljö och inkludering (KETEI)
Swedish Program for Kenya's Enhanced Trade Environment and Inclusion (KETEI)

description.narrative: A trade and development programme aimed at enhancing Kenya's national objectives in greening of border markets and infrastructure, development of climate-trade related regulatory frameworks, enhanced resilience of women and youth owned SME participation in trade and enhanced port competitiveness.

Ett handels- och utvecklingsprogram som syftar till att stärka Kenyas nationella mål för grönare gränsmarknader och infrastruktur, utveckling av klimatrelaterade regelverk för handel, ökad motståndskraft för kvinnors och ungdomars deltagande i handel genom små och medelstora företag samt förbättrad hamnkonkurrenskraft

Swedish Program for Kenya's Enhanced Trade Environment and Inclusion (KETEI) is designed to address critical policy, inclusion and environmental challenges in Kenya's trade arena. The goal of the program is: To promote inclusive and sustainable economic development in Kenya through increased green and inclusive export trade.
By the end of the program, KETEI is expected to contribute to the following specific objectives:
• Enhanced port performance? through improved operations efficiency through installation of smart gates solution through implementing a smart gate solution at Mombasa Port and Naivasha Inland Container Depot (ICD) and build a body of knowledge from the feasibility study for greening Mombasa Port and the Naivasha Dry Port that will examine e-mobility options to reduce emissions and enhance sustainability in port operations. • Promote trade inclusivity in Kenya. Through enhancing market access for SMEs especially those owned by women, youth and people with disabilities. • Establish strong connections between local SMEs and international buyers, creating sustainable linkages that enhance market access.

description.narrative:
The programme focused on groundwork for the project during the period under review. This included procurement, stakeholder sensitization as well as engaging government officials as partners.
Activities under the inclusive trade component however achieved the following results.
1. Activities to identify and support women entrepreneurs, cooperatives, and exporters in the mango, avocado, and vegetable value chains. A comprehensive mapping exercise was conducted to assess supply chains, evaluate compliance with international export standards, and categorize enterprises based on their operational scale. Stakeholder consultations were held with exporters, cooperatives, processors, financial institutions, and trade facilitation bodies to inform targeted interventions. Selection prioritized women led businesses already active in horticultural production, with demonstrated potential to scale into export markets.
2. Notable entities identified include Vert Limited, Hello Fresh Farm Limited, Iviani Farm, RTC Fruit Exporters, Makueni Fruit Processors, Kalamba Fruit Farmers, Kilungu Avocado Farmers Community Based Organization (CBO), and Kanoto Farmers Cooperative. Key challenges identified included low awareness of export standards, weak market linkages, and inadequate post harvest handling practices.
3. During the April to June 2025 quarter, implementation progressed with a focus on strengthening the capacity of women led and women dominated groups. A total of 64 farmer groups were identified and vetted, comprising 1,396 members: 1,263 women and 133 men. The selection criteria focused on women's leadership and decision making roles. This sets the stage for targeted training in export readiness, financial literacy, governance, and sustainable production practices.
4. A total of 20 training sessions were planned, two per sub county across 10 national government sub counties with each session expected to host approximately 55 participants. Coordination with national and county government structures is ongoing to ensure optimal geographic coverage and avoid duplication. Next steps include finalizing the training schedule and venue mapping, aligning session content and facilitation methodology, and developing tools to track gender dis aggregated outcomes.
5. Integration of a gender focused approach is to programming was achieved to drive inclusive trade by enhancing the capacity of women led enterprises to access and thrive in export oriented horticulture markets.
6. Interactive workshops with practical simulations and peer mentoring were conducted for the mango farmers. At least 50% of participants achieved export compliance certifications within six months, securing a minimum of 15 new export contracts or partnerships with regional buyers (e.g., via AfCFTA platforms).
Results will be updated following submission of the annual report in January. More results under the Enhanced Port Performance? and the Green Technology Solutions, enhanced green trade infrastructure and policy outcome areas will be reported in the coming year since all ground work has been completed and implementation has commenced
